around.headline: Bengaluru techie allegedly kills wife over WhatsApp voice-note dispute, dies by suicide
around.summary: A software engineer in Bengaluru allegedly killed his techie wife following a dispute that started over a WhatsApp voice note and a house-related argument, then died by suicide, police said. If you or someone you know is in an abusive relationship, the Karnataka women's helpline (1091) and police (112) can step in before a dispute escalates.
around.source: NDTV, India Today, The Times of India

around.headline: Auto driver tries to run over traffic policeman, held in Bengaluru
around.summary: An auto driver allegedly tried to run over a traffic policeman in the city and has been arrested. A reminder that assaulting on-duty traffic personnel is a serious criminal offence, not just a roadside dispute.

around.headline: Metro Green Line disrupted today; Blue Line deadline slips again to mid-2027
around.summary: Namma Metro's Green Line saw services disrupted today after BMRCL confirmed a technical glitch, capping off a rough post-Independence Day weekend that also saw the Blue Line's opening pushed again to mid-2027. Check BMRCL's live updates before heading out if you rely on the Green Line this evening.
around.source: Goodreturns, The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: CM's Independence Day speech promises 72,000 jobs, an AI university, a 'green Bengaluru' push
around.summary: Karnataka's Chief Minister used his Independence Day address to promise 72,000 new jobs, a dedicated AI university, and a green-Bengaluru drive among other big-ticket pledges. Worth watching for follow-through rather than expecting immediate change.

around.headline: FSSAI crackdown on expired food spreads beyond Bengaluru to Mysuru, Mangaluru
around.summary: FSSAI's crackdown on expired and unsafe food stock has widened from Bengaluru to hotels in Mysuru and Mangaluru. Worth checking expiry labels and asking eateries about their hygiene rating before eating out this week.

around.headline: Indonesia earthquake kills at least 53, aftershocks hamper rescue efforts
around.summary: A powerful earthquake in Indonesia has killed at least 53 people, with aftershocks slowing rescue work and thousands evacuating the affected area. Part of a run of major seismic activity in the region this year.

street_smart.title: A waiter takes your card to 'swipe it at the counter' and walks off with it for a couple of minutes. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds fit the choice-based trap format (today's real Bengaluru news — a murder-suicide, an auto driver held for trying to run over a traffic cop, a Metro glitch, the CM's I-Day promises, and an FSSAI food crackdown — doesn't lend itself to a 'best move' scenario). Rotating in from the evergreen list: credit-card skimming. This is the one evergreen topic that hasn't run in the last three weeks: phone snatching ran this morning (2026-08-16), loan-app harassment ran yesterday evening (2026-08-15), and UPI fraud (2026-08-10), fake job offers (2026-08-09), digital-arrest scams (2026-08-05), OTP/social engineering (2026-08-04), rental/tenant traps (2026-08-07), auto overcharging (2026-08-03), two-wheeler theft (2026-08-02) and medical emergencies (2026-08-11) have all appeared more recently too. The last card-skimming scenario ran 2026-07-26, just outside the three-week window — this one is framed at a restaurant POS counter instead of an ATM, to keep it distinct.
street_smart.situation: The bill hasn't come yet, your card is out of sight at the counter, and you have no way of knowing whether it's just being swiped — or skimmed — before it comes back.

choices.text: Say nothing, since letting staff carry your card off to the counter is completely normal in India.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Skimming devices are small, cheap, and fast — a distracted second at an unattended counter is all it takes to clone your card's data, and you'd have no way to know it happened.

choices.text: Insist the card machine be brought to your table instead, so the transaction happens in front of you and you can watch the whole swipe.
choices.feedback: Correct. Most restaurants and shops in Bengaluru now carry portable POS machines — asking for one keeps your card in your sight the entire time, which is the single biggest defence against skimming.

choices.text: Follow the waiter to the counter and watch him swipe it, but don't bother checking the receipt or your bank's SMS/app alert afterward.
choices.feedback: Watching the swipe is good, but skipping the follow-up leaves a gap — always check the receipt's masked card number and amount, and confirm the transaction alert on your phone matches before you relax.

choices.text: Loudly accuse the staff of trying to scam you and demand a manager before anything is swiped.
choices.feedback: There's no evidence of wrongdoing yet, and escalating first can turn a routine ask into an unnecessary confrontation. Calmly requesting a portable machine gets you the same protection without the scene.

takeaways: Ask for a portable POS machine at the table wherever possible, so your card never leaves your sight.
Turn on SMS/app transaction alerts on your card so any unauthorized swipe pings you within seconds.
If you spot an unfamiliar transaction, call your bank's 24x7 card-blocking number immediately and report it at cybercrime.gov.in or by dialling 1930.

quiz.why: The Blue Line will connect the airport to the ORR corridor via KR Puram, and delays have largely been blamed on pending civil works along the Outer Ring Road stretch.

quiz.why: The speech also announced a dedicated AI university and a 'green Bengaluru' push as part of the same set of pledges.

quiz.question: The earthquake that struck Indonesia this weekend, triggering mass evacuations, has killed at least how many people?
quiz.why: Indonesia sits on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire', a horseshoe-shaped zone responsible for around 90% of the world's earthquakes.

quiz.question: The Indian Constitution formally came into force on:
quiz.why: 26 November 1949 is when the Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly; it took effect two months later on 26 January, now celebrated as Republic Day.

quiz.question: The RBI's 'repo rate' is the interest rate at which:
options: The RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
Commercial banks lend to each other overnight
The government borrows directly from the RBI
quiz.why: The opposite transaction — the rate the RBI pays banks to park surplus funds with it — is called the reverse repo rate.
